> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/object.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3c06fc53ae2294d7bc5293ac6584d937f1dc1b30` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `33ee64dc1e63dc7445c59f6aac0fc5951719d883` — the merge of head `eabd7836377e3082d4592485d3ffd5b198620605` into base `3c06fc53ae2294d7bc5293ac6584d937f1dc1b30`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 33ee64dc1e63dc7445c59f6aac0fc5951719d883 && git checkout 33ee64dc1e63dc7445c59f6aac0fc5951719d883
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3c06fc53ae2294d7bc5293ac6584d937f1dc1b30 eabd7836377e3082d4592485d3ffd5b198620605 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3c06fc53ae2294d7bc5293ac6584d937f1dc1b30 && git merge --no-ff eabd7836377e3082d4592485d3ffd5b198620605

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3c06fc53ae2294d7bc5293ac6584d937f1dc1b30
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3c06fc53ae2294d7bc5293ac6584d937f1dc1b30` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 · PR #36096 · head `88f1d55e62` · **ACCEPT** · 2026-11-21T14:53Z

Card #35619, ruling 7035537883 (enforce). Re-filed claim 7064417927 (Clause-② yes: the new public `isObjectExportOffered` in `@object-ui/core`). Reports 7063246126 and 7064393903. I read the whole diff against `8145424b53`, 22 files, +569/−42. The PR declares Clause-② yes and Metadata-protocol semantic.

### What holds
- **One verdict, one home.** `isObjectExportOffered(obj, ops)` is `resolveEffectiveCrudAffordances(obj, ops).exportCsv`, so the authored `userActions.exportCsv` over the `managedBy` default (ADR-0103 opens export in every bucket) is ANDed with the effective `export` operation in the module that already owns the affordance resolution. No surface re-derives it.
- **Every Export entry reads it:**
  - `ObjectGrid` gates the toolbar Export menu, the handler itself (`if (!objectExportOffered) return;`), and the table's own CSV button (`exportable: operations?.export && objectExportOffered`), so `operations.export: true` cannot reopen it;
  - `ListView` gates the wide toolbar button, the Display panel footer and the handler through one `exportPermitted`;
  - `ReportExportControl` reads the base object's definition through the report's data source (`DatasetReportRenderer` now hands `dataSource` down) and replaces the bare `ops.includes('export')` with the same verdict;
  - `RelatedList` renders no export entry (`exportable: false`), so there is nothing to gate there, and the liveness note says so.
- **No `AFFORDANCE_GRANTS` row, correctly.** Export is a read: `can(object, 'export')` would read `allowRead`, while the caller's export grant reaches the client as the effective `export` operation (`list` ∧ `allowExport`). The jsdoc and the changeset both say this, and the setting is described as hiding an entry, not refusing a request, which is what the code does (no server path changes).
- **Spec face is text only.** `object.zod.ts` changes the `exportCsv` describe, `object.form.ts` the help text, and the generated English form bundle in `platform-objects` follows. No shape changes.
- **Liveness.** `userActions.exportCsv` flips dead → live with evidence pointing at the three gated surfaces; the state-count file moves by one.
- **Pins and ablation.** Grid, list (on the shared harness, per ruling 6583487846, both toolbar forms) and report each pin hidden-when-`false`, with CONTROLs for absent and `true`; the grid also pins that a closing `userActions` on another verb leaves export open. `managedBy.test.ts` adds five cases on the helper, including the effective-set AND (no `export` closes it; with `export` the authored bit stands) and the per-bucket equality with the resolved bit. The ablation `return true ||` in `isObjectExportOffered` turns 7 pins red, and every CONTROL stays green, so the pins discriminate.
- **Changeset.** I checked it sentence by sentence against the diff. The surfaces, the "not a permission" line, the report's fallback, the untouched translated locales and the `liveness-dead-property` consequence all match. The bumps are `minor` on spec and the four ui packages and `patch` on `platform-objects` (generated bundle only).
- **Scope.** Every file is inside claim 7064417927.
- **CI at `88f1d55e62`:** 63 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure.

### Nits (no re-review needed)
- **N1.** The report's Export control shows while the base definition is still being read, and stays when the source cannot serve one. The changeset and jsdoc say so and it is fail-open on a setting that is not a permission, so I accept it, but a report on an `exportCsv: false` object can briefly flash the control on first paint.
- **N2.** `scripts/pm/overlap-check` exits 1 against #35923. The overlap is on generated artifacts only (form bundle, liveness counts); whichever lands second regenerates.

### Owed
- **CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2:** the face is published schema (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, describe text). c-35619 runs it.
- Tier H via the seat after the L2, if the seat's rule applies.

## Contract review brief — PR #36096 @ `88f1d55e62e341ed33ba6bc3c7eb9b7231b8e68b` (card #35619)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #35619: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #36096: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `88f1d55e62e341ed33ba6bc3c7eb9b7231b8e68b`
  · the check-runs on `88f1d55e62e341ed33ba6bc3c7eb9b7231b8e68b`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts

  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission

  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or

  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/62d61432-ce68-559d-901c-e1f9805bf527/scratchpad/pr-36096/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches

     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `88f1d55e62e341ed33ba6bc3c7eb9b7231b8e68b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + ui/packages/core/src/utils/managedBy.ts, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-report/src/ReportExport.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-report/src/DatasetReportRenderer.tsx, packages/spec/liveness/object.json
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Card #35619, ruling 7035537883 (enforce). Read: the card and its six comments, the PR body and its 22-file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `8145424b`), and the 74 check-runs on this head (63 success, 11 skipped, none red, none pending). Code outside the diff was read in the tree at this head to judge the claims; it was not reviewed.

One graded finding is open on this head (S1, under ④): the new describe claims more than the code gates. Four nits beside it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged. Right.** `userActions.exportCsv` is `z.boolean().optional()` on both sides of the diff. Only its `.describe()` and the form row's `helpText` move. Nothing an author can write is added or refused.
- **Public surface: one new name. Right.** `isObjectExportOffered` is declared in `ui/packages/core/src/utils/managedBy.ts`, which `ui/packages/core/src/index.ts` re-exports whole; `origin/main` has no hit for the name. `ReportExportControlProps.dataSource` is not public: `ui/packages/plugin-report/src/index.tsx` re-exports nothing from `ReportExport.tsx`.
- **Meaning of an authorable key changes. Right.** An authored `exportCsv: false` goes from no effect to hiding the console entry. No default moves: `CRUD_AFFORDANCE_DEFAULTS` is untouched and no `authorable-defaults` shard is in the diff.
- **No server reader is added. Right.** `git grep exportCsv` over `packages/` outside `packages/spec` finds the FLS reference table in `metadata-core` (`exportCsv: keep`), a comment in `plugin-auth` and the generated translation bundles. The REST export door (`enforceExportPermission`) and the `/me/permissions` `apiOperations` derivation are not in the diff. So "refuses no export request" is true.
- **Liveness row `dead` to `live`. Right.** `evidenceScope: in-repo` is the right value (the ledger README: `in-repo` covers `ui/`). The four `file#symbol` anchors all resolve at this head, and `Spec property liveness` is green. `os lint` stops raising `liveness-dead-property` on an authored `exportCsv: true`.
- **Generated artifacts follow. Right.** The reference row in `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`, `state-counts/object.md` and the English `metadata-forms` bundle are regenerated, their gates are green, and no copy of the old describe is left in the tree.
- **One implied change the changeset does not name. Wrong in the changeset, right in the code.** ObjectGrid's table CSV button (`exportable`) read only `operations.export` before. It now also follows the effective `export` operation. See N2.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/35619-user-actions-export-csv-enforced.md` grades spec, `@object-ui/core` and the three ui plugins `minor`, and platform-objects `patch`. A `semantic` kind owes at least one moved package `minor` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3; `check-changeset-no-major`): met. A new public name on `@object-ui/core` is `minor`: met. platform-objects moves only a generated bundle, so `patch` is right. All six packages sit in the one `fixed` group.
- `Clause-②: yes` with no arm is right: the public surface grows by one name, and the accept set neither widens nor narrows. The line and `Metadata-protocol: semantic` stand line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body.
- The changeset declares nothing breaking (no `!`, no narrowing arm), so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. "Nothing needs migrating" holds: an object that authored `false` now gets what it wrote.
- `Check Changeset` is green on both of its runs.
- Two sentences of the changeset body are inaccurate: N2.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags from reports 7063246126 and 7064393903 and the PR's Acceptance notes, each answered:

- **RelatedList untouched, though the ruling names it.** Accepted. At this head `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx` has no export control, draws its table with `exportable: false`, and builds its enlarged `object-grid` node with neither `exportOptions` nor `operations`. An entry added there later would pass through ObjectGrid's gate. The card's defect text listed a menu that does not exist.
- **Open while the object definition loads.** Accepted for the grid and the list: it is the stance of every sibling gate in `ObjectGrid.tsx` (its own comment says so), and an embed with no object must stay open. For the report see N1.
- **Table CSV button now follows the effective `export` operation.** Accepted. It is the gate the toolbar menu beside it already applied, and it stops a client-side CSV of loaded rows for a viewer whose permission sets grant no export. It is permission-adjacent and was not on the card, which is one reason the security line in the header reads `yes`; the other is that the changed describe, help text and docblocks teach who may export. The changeset should name it (N2).
- **Legacy `ReportViewer` untouched.** Accepted. It reads `schema.report`, `schema.data` and its own `allowExport`, and binds no object.
- **A helper, not an `AFFORDANCE_GRANTS` row.** Accepted, each leg read. `MePermissionsProvider` maps `export` to `allowRead`. `annotateEffectiveApiOperations` derives `export` from list ∧ `allowExport`. The census in `affordanceGrantMap-12082.test.tsx` matches write verbs and the two CRUD policy readers. An export-only helper cannot return a write bit, so the census loses nothing. The census text does not yet name this third reader; that is a line for whoever next edits that file.
- **ListView pin in the shared harness.** Accepted: AGENTS.md, ruling record 6583487846.
- **Overlap with #35923 on two generated files.** Accepted. Whichever lands second regenerates them, and a regeneration-only hop keeps this record.
- **Interim text in `.changeset/35401-user-actions-transfer.md`.** Stays with the seat. Both changesets are unreleased on `main`, and that one still says the key is dead and warns. Shipped in one release they print two opposite paragraphs in one CHANGELOG, so the seat's amendment is owed before the release is cut.
- **Ten translated help texts kept.** Accepted. They are narrower than the English text ("CSV export entry"), not false. Translation follow-up.
- **Claim line read `Clause-②: no`.** Closed: re-filed `yes` in 7064417927.
- `open_questions` is empty in both reports. The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no off-relay note is owed.

Raised by this review, for the maintainer's approval line and not a finding: the decision card he answered called this the 「禁止导出 CSV」 switch. What lands hides the console entry and refuses nothing on the server. `GET /data/:object/export` still answers a caller who holds `allowExport`, and SDK and MCP callers are untouched. That matches the card's Done-when and ADR-0103 (an affordance, not authorization), and the PR's speed-read says it in its third line. His approval should be given on that reading.

SQL push-down: no query path is in the diff. The one added read is a by-name `getObjectSchema` through the adapter's metadata cache. No id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix.

**S1 (should-fix) — the describe, the help text and the helper's docblock claim every Export entry and every format, and the Gantt view's own Export buttons are outside the gate.**

`object.zod.ts` now says: "Show the Export entry (every format, not only CSV) on this object's grids, list views and reports; false hides it." `object.form.ts` says the same in the Studio help text, and the `isObjectExportOffered` docblock says every Export entry reads the helper. At this head `ui/packages/plugin-gantt/src/GanttView.tsx` draws two toolbar buttons, `gantt-export-png` ("Export as PNG") and `gantt-export-pdf` ("Export PDF"), with no condition at all: no `exportOptions`, no effective operation, no `isObjectExportOffered`. `ListView` renders that component as `object-gantt` for an object's `viewType: gantt`. So on an object that authors `exportCsv: false`, its Gantt list view still offers two Export entries, in formats the sentence says are covered. This is the gap the card was filed to close, in one remaining corner (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 10: keep the claim as narrow as the enforcement, and check every call site).

Two ways to close it:
